what: Round 1509. Who plays the Europa League in today's world (2026-27 on): each modern European league's Europa League places as UEFA's 2026/27 access list gives them beside the game's own LEAGUE_RULES row, the cup route and its pass down, the two holder routes, the real 2025-26 cup winners and Conference League winner that season one reads, and the competition's shape and nights. Held as DATA with the pages it was read from. src/lib/euroAccess.ts states these numbers and scripts/simWorldEuro.mjs section 0 fails if the two disagree.
rules: verified needs two sources from two publishers on two hosts, none a wiki. UEFA's regulations and uefa.com are one publisher.
onePublisher and toVerify rows are marked, never filled, and no constant may stand on them: their usedBy list is empty and section 0 holds that.

An access row (A) agrees when the real 2026/27 access list gives its league the game's Champions League places (qualifying routes counted as in, the game's own convention) and exactly the game's Europa League league places, plus the cup winner. A row that is not verified or does not agree is named in EURO_ACCESS_PARTIAL, and the game's places for that league are its simplification, said on the screen.
A literal is a line the page reader or the search engine quoted from the page on the read day. A figure a row states is printed by two of its publishers, each in a line about that figure.
A source that only repeats another's text counts once.

accessList.publisher: Bert Kassies, UEFA coefficients (kassiesa.net), Access List 2026/27, version v7.2
accessList.header: Rank Assoc League Stage POnc Q3nc Q2nc PO Q3 Q2 Q1 League Stage PO Q3 Q2 Q1 Q3ch
accessList.reading: The reader printed each association's row with its blank cells dropped, so a cell's column is read off the page order: the Champions League's columns come first, then the Europa League's (its league stage first), then the Conference League's. A cell holding CW (the cup winner) that UEFA's own list shows in the Europa League league phase fixes where the Europa League columns start.

rows.fact: England 2026/27: five Champions League places (the fifth a European Performance Spot), the cup winner and sixth place in the Europa League.
rows.note: The European Performance Spot is a one year bonus (the Premier League's own explainer). The game keeps the four place core, so its Europa League place is fifth where 2026/27's was sixth: the game's simplification.

literal: UEFA member associations (hereinafter associations) may enter the winner of their national cup competitions
one representative: the winner of the domestic cup;

The fifth-placed team in the Premier League qualify for the league phase

rows.fact: A cup winner already qualified through its league (for the Champions League, or for the Europa League by its place) hands the cup's place down its league to the next club not already qualified.

sources.publisher: UEFA, Regulations of the UEFA Europa League 2026/27, Articles 3.03 and 3.04
literal: If the winner of the domestic cup qualifies for the UEFA Champions League via the domestic championship
The highest-ranking domestic championship club not qualifying for the UEFA Champions League or UEFA Europa League
If a domestic cup winner that automatically qualifies for the UEFA Europa League also qualifies for the UEFA Europa League via its domestic championship,

The highest-ranking domestic championship club not qualifying for the UEFA Europa League enters the UEFA Europa League at the stage initially reserved for the association's lowest-ranking qualifying domestic championship club.
If the FA Cup winners finish in the top five of the Premier League,
their UEL league-phase place will go to the next-highest ranked team not qualified for UEFA competitions

rows.fact: Two legs in the knockout play-offs, the round of 16, the quarter-finals and the semi-finals, then a one match final.
rows.note: The game settles a level tie the way its Champions League does (extra time, then penalties), the engine comment's rule.

rows.fact: The 2026/27 Europa League's seventeen nights in their real months: September, October, October, November, November, December, January, January (the league phase), February twice, March twice, April three times, May twice (the knockouts and the final). The game's own dates sit on its calendar; this row only holds the order of the months.
